funFacts.text: Their nape and upperparts to the upper rump are light olive with a buffy tinge and dusky centers to the feathers that give a streaked appearance.
The sulphur-bellied flycatcher feeds on insects year-round and in the non-breeding season adds much fruit to its diet.
The female alone builds the nest in a tree cavity, either natural or excavated by a woodpecker.
Its "screech" call has been compared to "the protest of a wagon wheel that needs oiling".

summary: The sulphur-bellied flycatcher (Myiodynastes luteiventris) is a large member of the family Tyrannidae, the tyrant flycatchers. It is regularly found from southern Arizona in the United States south to Bolivia and occurs casually or as a vagrant further north, east, and south of its usual range.

The sulphur-bellied flycatcher is monotypic. Because there is much clinal variation in size and plumage, several subspecies have been proposed but not accepted. The sulphur-bellied flycatcher and the streaked flycatcher (M. maculatus) are sister species.
